announcements.title: Nominate the PROFessional(s) of the Month
announcements.full_body:
PROFessional(s) of the Month is for faculty, staff, or employee groups at any level across all University campuses. The monthly recipient(s), chosen by the Employee Recognition Committee, will receive a special visit by this group of professionals dedicated to recognizing—and celebrating—outstanding work by Rowan employees.

Which Rowan professional or team of professionals has gone beyond the call of duty in serving the University community? Who in the past month exhibited terrific employee and/or student engagement, customer service, and teamwork, exemplifying all that is exceptional about Rowan professionals? 

In short, who should be Rowan’s PROFessional(s) of the Month? 

View past honorees: PROFessionals of the Month 

Nominations can be submitted for individual employees, work groups or project teams. The ideal candidate(s) will have played a major role in a recent, exceptional accomplishment, preferably in or just prior to the month they have been nominated for (Examples: Completion of a high impact task or project, successful organization of an event, receipt of an award for an extraordinary accomplishment, etc.).   

To nominate faculty, staff, or a team of professionals for the PROFessional(s) of the Month, fill out this form by the end of the calendar month to explain why your nominee(s) should be recognized. Feel free to re-submit nominations that were previously submitted!

announcements.title: Provost's Town Hall - Oct 14
announcements.full_body:
Provost’s Town Hall & Social

We welcome all faculty, staff, and managers to join us for a Town Hall on Wednesday, October 14, 2026, where Provost Voki Pophristic will share Academic/Student Affairs updates and open the floor to questions. Following the session and Q&A, we invite you to stay to enjoy some light refreshments, build connections, and explore opportunities for collaboration.

Register Here so that we can plan for seating and refreshments. 

Date: Wednesday, October 14, 2026

Times: 

  • 10:00 - 11:15 - Presentation and Q&A
  • 11:15 - 12:00 - Social

Location: Hybrid

  • Chamberlain Student Center, Eynon Ballroom (in-person preferred)
  • WebEx (Register for the link)

Who:  This event is open to all faculty, staff, and managers

If there are any topics you would like to hear about during the Town Hall, please feel free to submit them anonymously here. Voki will do her best to incorporate what she can during the presentation. Additionally, we will have an open Q&A session at the end of the Town Hall.  

Questions about this event can be directed to Sarah Fobes at redacted@example.invalid.

announcements.title: Provost’s Coffee Hours (Focus on Research)
announcements.full_body:
Provost’s Coffee Hours (Focus on Research)

Provost’s Coffee Hours are dedicated times to engage in small-group conversations with the Provost -- to ask questions, discuss issues, and exchange ideas about Rowan initiatives. Attendees are encouraged to take insights back to their colleagues and departments, and the Provost will use what emerges in these conversations to inform ongoing work. 

Light refreshments are provided.

Our August sessions will be focused on research. The dates are:

  • Thursday, September 10 from 11:00-12:30 
  • Monday, September 21 from 2:30-4:00

If you are interested in attending one of these coffee hours, we invite you to register your interest by completing this form (go.rowan.edu/CoffeeSept26) by Monday, September 7th. These sessions are limited to 10-12 people and we will try to balance participation across colleges and units. 

There will be additional coffee hours throughout the year with different focus areas. Be sure to look out for additional announcements!

announcements.title: *Reminders and Updates: Office of Student Equity & Compliance
announcements.full_body:
As we begin the new academic year, the Office of Student Equity and Compliance (OSEC) reminds all students, faculty, and staff of the policies that help promote a safe, respectful, and inclusive community. We encourage you to review the policies below and become familiar with the protections, rights, and responsibilities that may apply to you in your role at Rowan.

Title IX Sexual Harassment/Sexual Assault: Protects students and employees  from certain forms of sexual harassment and sexual assault and outlines the University’s process for addressing conduct covered by Title IX.

Student Sexual Misconduct and Harassment Policy: Prohibits sexual misconduct and harassment involving students that may fall outside the scope of the Title IX policy and establishes procedures for responding to these concerns.

Pregnancy and Related Conditions Policy: Protects students who are pregnant or experiencing pregnancy-related conditions and provides for reasonable modifications, support, and other protections to help students remain engaged in their academic programs.

Policy Prohibiting Discrimination in the Workplace and Educational Environment: Prohibits discrimination and harassment based on protected characteristics and establishes the University’s process for addressing concerns involving discrimination in the workplace or educational environment.

If you have questions about these policies, your rights, or how to report a concern, the Office of Student Equity and Compliance is available to assist you. Beginning Fall 2026, we have a new campus location and can be found in Memorial Hall, Suite 157.

announcements.title: Student-Led Discussion of "Comparing Strategic and Systemic Periods of Starvation" RCHGHR
announcements.full_body:
Student-Led Discussion of “Comparing Strategic and Systemic Periods of Starvation” 

Wednesday 30 September 2026 from 3:30-4:30 in Chamberlain Student Center 127

RCHGHR Student Association

The Rowan Center for the Study of the Holocaust, Genocide, and Human Rights Student Association, Model Diplomacy Organization, UNICEF, and Ric Edelman College invite you to join us for a student-led discussion about “Comparing Strategic and Systemic Periods of Starvation” on 30 September at 3:30pm in CSC 127. Join the RCHGHR Student Association to discuss the history of different periods of time in which the governing body purposefully withheld food to civilians, such as the Holodomor and the Bengal Famine. There will be time at the end of the event for questions and comments led by our RCHGHR Student Association President Anna Cherian. Co-Sponsored by Model Diplomacy Organization, UNICEF, and Ric Edelman College of Communication, Humanities & Social Sciences - led by RCHGHR Student Association. Please join us for this important event on Wednesday 30 September 2026 at 3:30pm in CSC 127. All are welcome!

announcements.title: September 11 Memorial Service — 25th Anniversary
announcements.full_body:
September 11 Memorial Service — 25th Anniversary

On the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 attacks, Rowan Catholic invites the entire Rowan University community to join us for a memorial service as we remember those who lost their lives and honor the courage and sacrifice of the first responders and all those affected by the events of September 11.

Please join us in remembrance and prayer as we come together as a community on this important anniversary.

Friday, September 11, 2026
6:00 p.m.
September 11 Memorial, Rowan University

All members of the Rowan community are welcome.

Student can meet at 5:30 pm at the Newman House and walk to the 9/11 Memorial for the service.

announcements.title: Hollybush Tour
announcements.full_body: Step inside Hollybush Mansion and explore history in our own backyard. Hollybush tells three connected stories: the early history of Glassboro and its glassmaking heritage under the Whitney family, the University’s history through the legacy of its presidents, and the 1967 summit between President Lyndon B. Johnson and Soviet Premier Alexei Kosygin. Our tour guides  bring these histories to life, connecting the past to the people and community of today. Whether you are a student, employee, or neighbor, visiting Hollybush is an opportunity to take pride in Rowan’s roots and understand its place in the wider world.
